summary: A single field for date and time: typeable segments and one popover with a calendar, time list, shortcuts, and a “Now” button.
whenToUse: Appointments, bookings, scheduled publishing: date and time in a single field.
Fixed-step time slots (15/30/60 min) with unavailable times.
whenNotToUse: Time only: use TimePicker (with a list) or TimeInput (segments only).

props.name: value / defaultValue / onChange
props.description: Civil date and time or zoned instant: the time zone is preserved.

props.name: timeStep
props.description: Step in minutes for the time list. The field still accepts any typed time.

props.name: isTimeUnavailable
props.description: Disables individual times in the list.

props.name: minValue / maxValue / isDateUnavailable
props.description: Constraints; on the minimum/maximum day, out-of-range times are disabled.

props.name: presets
props.description: Shortcuts (Today, Tomorrow, In a week, or custom); they keep the selected time.

props.name: showMonthYearPicker
props.description: Month and year selectors in the calendar header.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description: Forces the hour format (follows the locale by default).

inherits: react-aria-components DatePicker props (name, isRequired, validate, hideTimeZone, firstDayOfWeek…).

keyboard.action: Next segment, then the field buttons.
Moves the day or time; Enter selects.
Closes the popover; focus returns to the field.

accessibility: The popover is a dialog with a calendar (grid) and a time list (listbox “Choose time”), labeled and localized.
Unavailable times are aria-disabled and skipped during navigation.
The popover does not close when a day is chosen: confirm with a time, “Done”, “Now”, or Esc.
responsive: Above 40rem the calendar and time list sit side by side; below, the times move under the calendar and the shortcuts become scrollable chips.
customization: className on the field, popoverProps.className on the popover; colors and radii from --dc-* tokens.
commonMistakes: Using ZonedDateTime for “wall clock” times (e.g. store opening): use CalendarDateTime.
Expecting timeStep to prevent off-step times: it only limits the list; validate with validate if needed.
Serializing a CalendarDateTime with toDate().toISOString(): use toString() or convert explicitly with toZoned().
limits: The time list shows hours and minutes: with granularity="second" seconds can only be adjusted via the segments.
